node: Export controls, sanctions, and procurement compliance software/services
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the export-controls/sanctions/procurement-compliance node. The clearest US-listed direct exposure found is Descartes Systems Group, whose Visual Compliance / denied-party-screening tools map tightly to export, trade, OFAC, and restricted-party workflows. Thomson Reuters and RELX are larger reference anchors with embedded denied-party, sanctions, KYC/AML, legal, and regulatory data assets, but their market caps and diversified businesses reduce purity. FiscalNote is retained only as a speculative shadow candidate: it has policy/regulatory/tariff intelligence relevance but current evidence is weaker for direct sanctions/export-control workflow monetization. External context supports the node-level hypothesis that policy volatility and defense supply-chain opacity raise administrative burden, especially below prime contractors. Layer 1B expands the universe around compliance workload created by tariffs, sanctions, export controls, denied-party screening, and defense-industrial supply-chain visibility. The strongest public-market mapping is not defense primes but niche trade-compliance data/software and advisory providers. Reference leaders include Thomson Reuters and RELX/LexisNexis because they own broad sanctions and restricted-party data platforms. The more underfollowed lane is Descartes Systems Group and FTI Consulting: Descartes has unusually direct exposure through denied-party screening and global trade compliance software, while FTI has services exposure to export-control and sanctions compliance programs.
